columns.name: id
columns.description: Surrogate primary key; unchanged from F1.

columns.name: sku
columns.description: Stock keeping unit; unchanged from F1. Half of the UNIQUE(sku, location) key (PI2).

columns.name: location
columns.description: Canonical storage location; unchanged from F1 and never overwritten from the code's leading segment (AC3, PI2). Half of UNIQUE(sku, location).

columns.name: quantity
columns.description: Filed quantity; carried through the refactor untouched so every pre-migration row survives (AC1/AC2, PI4).

columns.name: batch_number
columns.description: Batch segment split from the retired inventory_code (segment 2). NULLABLE by design (PI3): a nonconforming code leaves this NULL rather than being defaulted or dropping the row (AC2).

columns.name: serial_number
columns.description: Serial segment split from the retired inventory_code (segment 3). NULLABLE by design (PI3): a nonconforming code leaves this NULL (AC2).

columns.name: created_at
columns.description: Row creation timestamp; preserved across this migration (PI4).

columns.name: updated_at
columns.description: Last write timestamp; preserved across this migration (PI4).

schema_changes.detail: Add batch_number text NULL. NULLABLE with no default: nonconforming codes must land as NULL (PI3, AC2). This is the expand phase of an expand/contract split of inventory_code.
schema_changes.migration_note: upgrade() adds the column; downgrade() drops it. Reversible.

schema_changes.detail: Add serial_number text NULL. NULLABLE with no default (PI3, AC2). Expand phase.
schema_changes.migration_note: upgrade() adds the column; downgrade() drops it. Reversible.

schema_changes.detail: Backfill batch_number = segment 2 and serial_number = segment 3 of inventory_code, split on the '-' delimiter. Conforming codes (location-batch-serial) populate both columns (AC1); codes lacking a batch/serial segment leave both NULL (AC2). location is NOT read from the code's leading segment and is never rewritten (AC3). No row is dropped regardless of parse outcome (PI4). An integrity probe over the same parse rule counts unparseable rows for review before acceptance (AC5).
schema_changes.migration_note: Pure delimiter-parse data backfill executed in the same transaction as the add_column steps so add+backfill is atomic. downgrade() has no dedicated backfill step; reconstruction happens in the inventory_code re-add below. Delimiter-only parsing, no fabrication.

schema_changes.detail: Drop the inventory_code column. After add+backfill this is the contract phase: batch_number and serial_number become the first-class, separately queryable columns (AC4).
schema_changes.migration_note: REVERSIBILITY (PI1, AC6): downgrade() re-adds inventory_code text, then reconstructs each value from location + '-' + batch_number + '-' + serial_number (join rule mirrors the up-migration split rule), then drops serial_number and batch_number. up-then-down round-trips schema and every row; inventory_code is temporarily backfilled NOT NULL only after reconstruction if F1's NOT NULL is to be restored, else re-added NULL to tolerate rows that were nonconforming. Whole revision is one transaction.
